notes.note: Digits are now read as words, so the formula reads 'wāḥid Wāḥid · ithnān ithnān …' and 'khamsata ʿashara Khamsata ʿashara …' (digit and word both read, with a capital mid-line). Correct but odd; the digit could be skipped when the word follows.
The two-reading glosses repeat themselves: أَكْبَر = 'bigger; bigger, older; the biggest', أَغْلَى = 'more expensive; more expensive; the most expensive', أَقَلّ = 'less; less, fewer; the least'.
After لَيْسَ the ending is the predicate's -an, but the taps describe it as 'an indefinite object' / 'a feminine word as an object'. '(accusative ending: object, or after laysa/kāna)' would be exact.
مَعَ أَنَّ 'although' taps word by word as 'with' + 'that'; nowhere does the learner see 'although' on tap. A combined hint ('with: in maʿa anna = although') would help.
شِيكَاغُو taps as 'Chicago; Chicago (city in the USA)': duplicated reading.
يَنْزِلُ in يَنْزِلُ الثَّلْج (snow falls) taps as 'gets off, gets out; goes down'; 'falls, comes down' would fit.
تَنْتَظِرَكَ = '(she) wait for you (to a man)': the subject is the bus (f); '(it, f) waits for you (after lan)' reads better.
مَعَكَ حَقّ is colloquial-leaning (repeat from round 2); MSA prefers مَعَكَ الْحَقُّ or أَنْتَ عَلَى حَقّ.

summary: I read the whole grammar export (78 cards, 3,066 lines): every Arabic line, harakat and case ending, formula, table cell, explanation, example, translation and transliteration, and every tap gloss. I checked 704 Arabic strings (lines with a ⟶ reading) and 3,182 tap glosses on 701 tap lines. The Arabic itself is clean: no wrong harakat, case endings, agreement, conjugation or mood errors (inna/kāna/laysa/lam/lan/an/law, dual, numbers, iḍāfa, hollow verbs, imperatives, passive all correct); 0 Arabic strings wrong apart from 3 engine patterns in their transliteration. Most round-2 fixes held (mā, inna, comparatives, passive, السَّاعَةَ, كَرِيم, the dual rule, 11–99 in the explanation). I found 29 errors (5 major, 24 minor): 25 gloss, 1 grammar-fact, 3 engine; about 65 tap glosses (≈2%) are wrong or misleading. Patterns: (1) round-2 items only partly fixed or not fixed — أَفْعَلَ 'I do', ـِي 'my' on the feminine imperative, أَ 'present prefix', عَشَرَ 'part of fifteen', ذَهَب 'gold', قَلِيل 'a little (while)', تَشْرَبُوا 'after an', '11 and up' in the age table, إِنَّهُ still 'that he (after qāla)' in the inna lesson; (2) wrong person on ambiguous ta- forms (تَتَّصِلَ 'she', تَكُونُ/سَتَكُونُ in the أَنْتَ row, تَجْلِسُ 'she'); (3) one-sentence or idiomatic glosses leaking into grammar cards (عِنْدَ '(Daniel) has', حَاضِر 'certainly!', بِي 'bi (long i)'); (4) prefixes/helping vowels named as bare letters (اِ/اُ, مُـ); (5) engine: dropped unvocalised example and ؟, '-·hu', and inconsistent clitic hyphens.
